input: Scheduled routine: continue work on the repo aiming to develop, deploy, market, sell and support revenue generating software products (ventures brief)
task: New venture home-battery-planner: home battery replay on the household's own Green Button data and rate plans, self-powered / time-based / LP-checked perfect-foresight ceiling, size sweep, plan comparison

errors.what: First dynamic programme kept stored energy on a plain level grid and lost 3-4% of the optimal saving to quantization (spare solar could not be stored exactly); a test against a finer grid caught it.
errors.fix: Interpolated value-to-go plus the cost's bend points as candidate actions and a continuous-state forward pass; then checked against an exact HiGHS LP: within 0.21% on 32 full-year cases.

doc_friction.issue: Row 1 ai-bookkeeper's only BUILDABLE item needs huggingface.co, which allocate.py's own probe reported REFUSED this session; the latest 'left recently' reason said the same. Its parked NEXT.md items (Form 2210 Jan 31 rule, box D, 2026 draft) are already in penalty2210.mjs/annualized.mjs, so NEXT.md is stale there too.
Session-landing steps say open the PR as a draft and merge it yourself; the harness default says ready for review. Opened as draft as the claim, marked ready before merging.

deviations.why: 'Deepen a flagship by default': row 1 (ai-bookkeeper) had only a Hugging Face item and HF was refused; rows 2-8 had open PRs or long-tail sweeps (tennis-robot tach jitter, chant OMR glyphs) with little revenue upside. The owner's brief also asks to 'focus on starting new ones' with AI/algorithms and real business potential.
deviations.did: Started a new deep venture (home-battery-planner) in an energy niche the owner named a direction (industrial, energy, construction), with a real algorithm checked against an exact solver and a measurement on 40 real-weather homes.
deviations.result: Landed: tool page, guide, CLI, 31 tests, LP check, ResStock check, post.

goal: Ship a new revenue-path venture with depth (algorithm + real-weather measurement) and a marketing guide
notes: Local checks: node --test in ventures/home-battery-planner 31/31 pass (run_venture_tests.py home-battery-planner ok); check_posts ok; headless Chromium 1280/390 px, example runs ~1.3 s, no console errors, no horizontal scroll; venture-preflight output in PR body. Catalogue wiring: launched.json, HOUSEHOLD_SLUGS, optout-switches (sync_tree_counts.py), ventures/README.md regenerated by ventures-readme.mjs. No agent doc in docs/reports: the venture README carries everything the next run needs (model, checks, not checked, next steps in flagships-style 'Not checked').

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: an energy-modelling developer: ESPI/CSV meter reader with solar export, tariff DSL with holidays, three dispatch modes, interpolated DP and an independent LP check, ResStock pipeline and analysis, page, guide, CLI and tests

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
